idea: an app that provides you with the best plan(menu,  purchase plan) based on nutrition, cost, and time consumption. The app will use delivery data etc. to get the products and costs of goods. The user will be able to customize the plan based on their preferences.
pros: Addresses a growing market demand for convenient and personalized meal planning solutions, catering to health-conscious individuals and busy professionals seeking optimized nutrition, cost-effectiveness, and time savings.

Offers a competitive advantage by integrating real-time pricing and availability data from delivery services, ensuring accurate and up-to-date cost estimations and product accessibility. Feasibility is enhanced by leveraging readily available APIs from existing delivery platforms.

Provides a high degree of user customization, enabling individuals to tailor meal plans based on their dietary restrictions, allergies, preferred cuisines, and budget, enhancing user engagement and satisfaction.

Potentially fosters healthier eating habits by providing users with balanced and nutritious meal plans tailored to their specific needs, leading to improved health outcomes and reduced reliance on less healthy alternatives.
Streamlines the grocery shopping process by generating optimized purchase lists, reducing impulse buys, and minimizing food waste, resulting in cost savings and environmental benefits.
cons: Market demand challenges exist due to the presence of established competitors and the potential difficulty in acquiring and retaining users in a crowded meal planning app market. User acquisition costs could be high.

Data accuracy and reliability could be a significant challenge. Inaccurate pricing, availability, or nutritional information could lead to user frustration and app abandonment. Feasibility is hindered by the reliance on external APIs, which may be subject to change or limitations.

Personalization complexity presents a challenge. Effectively translating user preferences into accurate and satisfying meal plans requires sophisticated algorithms and a robust understanding of nutritional science. Developing and maintaining such algorithms is challenging and expensive.

Scalability issues may arise as the user base grows. Handling large volumes of data, processing numerous customization requests, and ensuring timely updates to pricing and availability information require robust infrastructure and efficient algorithms. Feasibility is questioned in handling the complexity and the computational burden.

Dependence on delivery service APIs poses a risk. Changes to API terms of service, functionality, or pricing by delivery providers could disrupt the app's core functionality and require costly re-engineering.
